name: @concordvoice/admin
//engines: node's floor was raised from the former 24.x by the jsdom 30 bump: jsdom@30 declares node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, so a plain 24.x advertised 24.0-24.14 as supported while the test environment was not. Advisory only — no .npmrc in this repo sets engine-strict — and CI is unaffected either way because setup-node's `node-version: 24` resolves the newest 24.x. The floor form is deliberate over ^24.15.0: it keeps Node 26 valid, which jsdom supports and which developers here actually run.
//overrides_security: brace-expansion@^5.0.9 closes GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (unbounded expansion -> OOM crash, first patched in 5.0.8 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.3) and GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation; first patched in 5.0.9 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.4); both transitive via eslint->minimatch. nanoid@^3.3.17 closes GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (custom generators loop indefinitely when size is zero; transitive via vite->postcss). undici has NO override here any more. jsdom is its ONLY consumer in this workspace, and jsdom@30 declares undici ^8.9.0 — which is exactly the 8.x first-patched floor for GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272, so that range cannot resolve to a vulnerable version and needs no pin to keep it out. The former undici@^7.29.0 entry closed that advisory on the 7.x line back when jsdom@29 declared ^7.25.0; against jsdom@30 the SAME entry forces a full major below what jsdom declares, which is why it is removed rather than retargeted. Note this is NOT the fast-uri case described below and does not license sweeping dormant entries: fast-uri was removed because it bound NOTHING, whereas undici binds jsdom's copy and the binding itself became the harm. Verify before reinstating: `npm ls undici --all` for the real consumer set, plus the per-line first_patched of EVERY undici advisory (`gh api /advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=undici`), not just one. minimatch@^10.2.5 REPLACES a former ^9.0.7 pin, which was a downgrade CAP (<10.0.0): eslint@10's chain requests minimatch ^10.2.x (^10.2.2 from @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree, ^10.2.4 from eslint and @eslint/config-array), and minimatch@9 is the version that calls brace-expansion's 2.x default export, dropped in 5.x — so the ^9 cap is what made brace-expansion@5 unreachable here. ^10.2.5 keeps an EXPLICIT floor above every 10.x minimatch advisory boundary (GHSA-7r86-cg39-jmmj and GHSA-23c5-xmqv-rm74 patch at 10.2.3, GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26 at 10.2.1) rather than relying on the consumer union floor, whose weakest member (^10.2.2) sits below two of those boundaries. minimatch@10.2.5 declares brace-expansion ^5.0.5, satisfied by the ^5.0.9 above. Do not re-add a minimatch pin below 10. A former fast-uri override was removed here: this lockfile does not resolve fast-uri, so it bound nothing, and the npm-audit gate — which resolves live against this lockfile on every CI run — is the control that would catch a reintroduction. That was decided for fast-uri specifically, because its motivating advisory is closed AND it bound nothing. It is NOT a general instruction to prune: tar, @tootallnate/once, tmp, serialize-javascript, rollup and ws are dormant in this workspace too, predate this change, and were deliberately left alone rather than swept.
